# Settings

A server reads one TOML file, `oml.toml` by default (`--config <path>`), and the environment. The environment wins over the file, and the file wins over the defaults. An environment name is `OML_`, then the dotted key in capitals with `__` between the parts: `search.rerank.depth` becomes `OML_SEARCH__RERANK__DEPTH`.

*Generated by `scripts/gen_settings_reference.py`; edit the source, not this page. Keys come from `crates/bins/oml-server-lead/src/lib.rs`; words from `scripts/settings_notes.yaml`.*

A value that does not parse stops the server at start and names the key. Per-tenant policy, such as a workarea's review rules, is not a setting: an administrator changes it with the [CLI](../cli/reference.md).

## Server settings

| Key | Environment variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `postgres.url` | `OML_POSTGRES__URL` | none (required) | The connection string of the serving role, a Postgres role that owns nothing and holds only the privileges the server's statements need. |
| `postgres.owner_url` | `OML_POSTGRES__OWNER_URL` | none (required) | The connection string of the owner role. The server runs its migrations under it at start and serves under `postgres.url`. A start without it is refused as `postgres.role_split`. |
| `server.listen` | `OML_SERVER__LISTEN` | `127.0.0.1:8080` | The address of the API listener. |
| `kms.adapter` | `OML_KMS__ADAPTER` | the file keyring | Which key store wraps each memory's encryption key. This build has one, `file`, the keyring file; any other value stops the server at start. |
| `kms.keyring_path` | `OML_KMS__KEYRING_PATH` | `oml-keyring` | The keyring file, for the `file` adapter. Back it up with the database; a database restored without it cannot be read. |
| `oauth.issuer` | `OML_OAUTH__ISSUER` | unset (connections off) | The public origin of the server, `https` with no path and no trailing slash, such as `https://memory.example.com`. It turns on OAuth connections for claude.ai and the web pages. Set it to the address people reach, not the address the process binds behind its proxy. |
| `server.trusted_proxies` | `OML_SERVER__TRUSTED_PROXIES` | empty (no proxy trusted) | Addresses and CIDR ranges of reverse proxies, a TOML array in the file and comma-separated in the environment. Only a request from a listed peer has its client address read from `X-Forwarded-For`. Behind a proxy on the same host, set loopback. |
| `server.metrics_listen` | `OML_SERVER__METRICS_LISTEN` | unset (no metrics listener) | The address of a second listener that serves `GET /metrics` and nothing else, unauthenticated. Bind it where only the scraper reaches. The API listener never serves `/metrics`. |
| `server.otlp_endpoint` | `OML_SERVER__OTLP_ENDPOINT` | unset (no trace export) | The `http` or `https` base URL of an OpenTelemetry collector. The server posts spans to `<endpoint>/v1/traces` over OTLP with protobuf and sends no authentication header. |
| `web.google.client_id` | `OML_WEB__GOOGLE__CLIENT_ID` | unset (Google sign-in off) | The OAuth client ID of your Google application. Register the redirect URI `<oauth.issuer>/web/callback/google`. |
| `web.google.client_secret` | `OML_WEB__GOOGLE__CLIENT_SECRET` | unset | The matching secret. The server never logs it. Set both or neither. |
| `web.github.client_id` | `OML_WEB__GITHUB__CLIENT_ID` | unset (GitHub sign-in off) | The client ID of your GitHub OAuth app. Its callback is `<oauth.issuer>/web/callback/github`. |
| `web.github.client_secret` | `OML_WEB__GITHUB__CLIENT_SECRET` | unset | The matching secret. Set both or neither. The web pages need `oauth.issuer` and at least one provider. |
| `web.client_secret` | `OML_WEB__CLIENT_SECRET` | unset (no capacity credential accepted) | The secret `oml-web` sends as `OML-Web-Client` to present a person's capacity credential (`omls_`), at least 32 characters, set to the same value on the server and on `oml-web` (ADR-0070 d2). Unset, every capacity credential is refused as `auth.invalid` `session_outside_web` and `oml doctor` warns. The server never logs it. |
| `web.client_ca` | `OML_WEB__CLIENT_CA` | unset | Mutual TLS for `oml-web` (ADR-0070 d2) needs the server to terminate TLS on the listener `oml-web` reaches, which this build does not: setting it stops the server at start, naming the setting. Use `web.client_secret`. |
| `web.client_subject` | `OML_WEB__CLIENT_SUBJECT` | unset | The certificate subject `oml-web` presents under `web.client_ca`. Setting it stops the server at start in this build, as `web.client_ca` does. |
| `brief.max_tokens` | `OML_BRIEF__MAX_TOKENS` | `400` | The token budget a workarea's brief is cut to when an agent reads the workarea. The first member that does not fit ends the brief. |
| `signup.mode` | `OML_SIGNUP__MODE` | `allowlist`: the sign-in allowlist, unchanged | `open` lets a person whose provider-verified email no entry holds create an account after accepting the terms: a drawn user, a private root, `<user>-web` and `<user>-review` (ADR-0068 d1). `open` requires `oauth.issuer`, a sign-in provider (`web.google.*` or `web.github.*`) and every `signup.*` setting except `per_ip_per_hour`. A missing one, a tenant id that does not parse, or an issuer that is not a live admin key of that tenant stops the process at start, naming the setting. |
| `signup.tenant` | `OML_SIGNUP__TENANT` | unset | The tenant id sign-ups land in. Every person of that tenant is under the `quota.*` limits. |
| `signup.issuer` | `OML_SIGNUP__ISSUER` | unset | The name of an admin key of the sign-up tenant that adds each entry and issues its session keys. |
| `signup.terms_version` | `OML_SIGNUP__TERMS_VERSION` | unset | The terms version a person accepts, recorded on their entry and in `web.signed_up`. Changing it makes an open terms page refuse with `terms_version`. |
| `signup.terms_url` | `OML_SIGNUP__TERMS_URL` | unset | The terms page the terms checkbox links. |
| `signup.privacy_url` | `OML_SIGNUP__PRIVACY_URL` | unset | The privacy page the terms checkbox links. |
| `signup.per_ip_per_hour` | `OML_SIGNUP__PER_IP_PER_HOUR` | `5`, the operator's choice, unmeasured ([#164](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/issues/164)) | New accounts from one client address in a rolling hour, counted per process; an IPv6 address counts by its /64 and an IPv4 address by itself. The address is the request line's, so behind a proxy set `server.trusted_proxies`, or every sign-up shares one bucket (`oml doctor` warns). |
| `quota.memories` | `OML_QUOTA__MEMORIES` | `1000`, the operator's choice, unmeasured ([#164](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/issues/164)) | Live memories in a person's root, counted as chains, so a new version of a memory is not a new memory. Past it, `limit.quota`. An admin overrides one person's limit on `/web/admin/users`, journaled as `web.quota_set`. A value above 1,000,000 stops the start. |
| `quota.keys` | `OML_QUOTA__KEYS` | `5`, the operator's choice, unmeasured ([#164](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/issues/164)) | Live agent keys of a person. Past it, `limit.quota`. |
| `quota.connections` | `OML_QUOTA__CONNECTIONS` | `5`, the operator's choice, unmeasured ([#164](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/issues/164)) | Open connections of a person. Past it, `limit.quota`. |
| `quota.requests_per_minute` | `OML_QUOTA__REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE` | `120`, the operator's choice, unmeasured ([#164](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/issues/164)) | Requests per key per UTC minute, counted per process. Past it, `limit.rate`. |
| `search.enabled` | `OML_SEARCH__ENABLED` | `keyword-any`, `bm25`, `bm25-postings` | The search pipelines the server offers, a TOML array in the file and comma-separated in the environment. A request naming a pipeline that is not listed is refused with `request.validation`. |
| `search.default` | `OML_SEARCH__DEFAULT` | `bm25-postings` | The pipeline a recall uses when neither the request nor the tenant names one. It must be in `search.enabled`. Where the server loads the sparse model, `bm25-sparse` finds more and costs CPU at write time: see [which one to use](../architecture/retrieval.md#which-one-to-use). Removing a pipeline from `search.enabled` that a tenant chose as its default makes that tenant's recalls that name no pipeline fail with `settings.invalid` until its admin chooses another. |
| `search.rerank.model` | `OML_SEARCH__RERANK__MODEL` | `ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2` | The cross-encoder the reranking pipeline loads. This build pins `ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2` and `ms-marco-MiniLM-L4-v2`, both Apache-2.0. |
| `search.rerank.model_dir` | `OML_SEARCH__RERANK__MODEL_DIR` | `<state>/models/<model>` | An absolute directory holding `config.json`, `tokenizer.json` and `model.safetensors`. The server checks each file against a pinned SHA-256 and stops at start on a mismatch. |
| `search.rerank.fetch` | `OML_SEARCH__RERANK__FETCH` | `false` | `true` lets the server download missing model files at start from the pinned revision on Hugging Face and check each digest. `false` never uses the network. |
| `search.timings` | `OML_SEARCH__TIMINGS` | `false` | `true` lets a recall ask for each stage's milliseconds. Off by default because stage times over rows a key cannot read reveal how many there are. |
| `search.rerank.depth` | `OML_SEARCH__RERANK__DEPTH` | `10` | How many of the best candidates the cross-encoder reorders, 1 to 100. |
| `search.rerank.floor` | `OML_SEARCH__RERANK__FLOOR` | `off` | A relevance between 0 and 1 below which a reranked hit is withheld. A recall whose candidates all fall below it answers no hit and reports how many it withheld. |
| `search.rerank.max_concurrent` | `OML_SEARCH__RERANK__MAX_CONCURRENT` | `2` | Reranks that run at once. A recall that waits past its deadline for a slot serves the unreranked order and says why. |
| `search.rerank.timeout_ms` | `OML_SEARCH__RERANK__TIMEOUT_MS` | `1000` | The deadline of one rerank in milliseconds, waiting for a slot included. Past it the recall serves the unreranked order. |
| `search.rerank.threads` | `OML_SEARCH__RERANK__THREADS` | `2` | The threads of the reranker's own pool, shared by every rerank. |
| `search.rerank.max_tokens` | `OML_SEARCH__RERANK__MAX_TOKENS` | `256` | The longest query-and-passage pair the model reads, 64 to 512 tokens. |
| `search.sparse.model_dir` | `OML_SEARCH__SPARSE__MODEL_DIR` | `<state>/models/opensearch-neural-sparse-encoding-doc-v3-distill` | An absolute directory holding the sparse model's `config.json`, `tokenizer.json`, `model.safetensors` and `idf.json`. Read only when `search.enabled` names a sparse pipeline. |
| `search.sparse.fetch` | `OML_SEARCH__SPARSE__FETCH` | `false` | `true` lets the server download missing sparse-model files at start and check each digest. |
| `search.sparse.threads` | `OML_SEARCH__SPARSE__THREADS` | `2` | The threads of the sparse encoder's own pool. It writes each version's postings after the write commits, off the commit path. |

## Lake writer

The `oml-lakewriter` binary takes these as flags or environment variables. See [run the lake writer](lake.md).

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `OML_LAKE_URL` | none | The root of the lake, such as `file:///var/lib/oml/lake` or an object-store URL. Also the `--lake` flag. |
| `OML_LAKE_DATABASE_URL` | none | The connection string of the reader role the lake writer drains the outbox through. |
| `OML_LAKE_OWNER_URL` | none | The owner-role connection string, for the command that prepares the lake roles. |
| `OML_LAKE_KEK_FILE` | none | The key-encryption key file. The writer checks its permissions and age and warns when it is not given. |
| `OML_LAKE_METRICS_ADDR` | `127.0.0.1:9466` | The address of the lake writer's metrics listener. |

## Client and plugin

The CLI, the SDKs, the hooks and the agent kit read these. The Claude Code plugin reads its `url` and `api_key` options instead.

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `OML_URL` | The server's URL, without `/mcp`. Set with `OML_API_KEY` or not at all; a source that sets one alone is refused. |
| `OML_API_KEY` | The API key. Prefer it, or the credentials file `oml login` writes, to the `--api-key` flag, because argv is visible to other processes. |
| `OML_CLI_CREDENTIALS` | The path of the credentials file, for tests and for keeping several servers apart. |
| `OML_SESSION_CONTEXT` | `off` stops the session-start hook from loading the workarea's memory into a session. It takes `on` or `off`. |
| `OML_SESSION_CONTEXT_MAX_TOKENS` | The token budget of the session-start recall, an integer from 1 up. |
| `OML_FAILURE_RECALL` | `1` makes the plugin recall memories matching the error words after a failed command. Off by default. |
| `OML_TURN_RECALL` | `1` makes the plugin recall on every prompt, within its budget. Off by default. |
| `OML_METRICS_URL` | The lead's metrics listener, so that `oml doctor` can read rerank skips, scan findings and recall telemetry. |
